cells.title: Overview
cells.source: Model **ABM-PC** is Godley and Lavoie Model PC populated by many households. Each household holds cash and bills, earns wage and interest income, and has its own propensity to consume. Macro totals emerge by summing over agents. This notebook runs a Monte Carlo of that agent-based model in the browser from a YAML-authored `abm-model` cell. The R reference is `references/leeds_lectures_2026/ABM_PC.R`.
cells.more:
Aggregate and IO models are **top-down**: they write economy-wide behavioural
rules directly. **Agent-based models (ABMs)** are **bottom-up**: they specify
many individual agents — here households — and obtain macro variables by
_summing over agents_. Aggregate regularities then **emerge** from interaction
rather than being imposed.

Relative to ABM-SIM, Model PC adds a **portfolio choice** between bills and
cash, and interest income on bills. Taxes fall on labour _and_ interest.
The baseline experiment raises the policy rate from `2.5%` to `3.5%` at
period `60`, which shifts household wealth toward bills.

The model remains **stock-flow consistent**: household cash `H_h` tracks
central-bank cash supply `H_s`, and government bills satisfy
`B_s = B_h + B_cb`. Charts show Monte Carlo **means** with p10–p90 bands.

cells.title: ABM-PC specification
cells.description: Declarative agent-based PC: heterogeneous households, job lottery, FCFS goods market, bill/cash portfolio. Tick order matches Leeds ABM_PC.R. Upper-case names are MACRO totals (Monte Carlo means); lower-case / `*_h*` names are MICRO histories from MC run 1 only.
cells.more:
**Macro vs micro (Leeds convention).** The R script comments
`upper-case = MACRO total; lower-case = MICRO (one household)`.

- **Macro**: every aggregate tick variable is stored automatically as a Monte
  Carlo mean (banded p10–p90).
- **Micro**: first and last household, all state variables, from **MC run 1
  only** (not averaged) — `c_h1`, `v_hLast`, ….
- **MC count**: set on the run cell as `abm.monteCarlo` (not on the model).

Stock-flow check: `|H_h - H_s|` must stay within `tolerance` every period.

cells.title: Period ticks
cells.source: One period unfolds as the ordered tick list in the ABM-PC specification above: plan consumption, hire via a job lottery, shuffle the queue, serve government then households first-come-first-served, pay wages and interest taxes, update wealth, and allocate the portfolio between bills and cash. The policy rate rises from `2.5%` to `3.5%` at period `60`.
cells.more:
Conventions: upper-case = MACRO total; lower-case = one household (MICRO).

1. Each household plans `cd = min(max(alpha1 * yd + alpha2 * v, 0), v)` using its
   own `alpha1` and last period's disposable income and wealth.
2. Aggregate demand is `AD = sum(cd) + G`. Labour needed is `Nd = AD / pr`.
3. Hiring: `N = min(floor(Nd * random.uniform(1-s, 1+s, 1)), floor(Nd), households.size)`.
4. One random shuffle orders both jobs and the shop queue.
5. Government is served first; remaining output is rationed FCFS to households.
6. Hired households earn wage `w = pr`. Interest `lag(r) * lag(b)` is taxed with
   labour income at rate `theta`. Wealth updates as `v = v - c + yd`.
7. Portfolio: `b = v * (lambda0 + lambda1 * r) - lambda2 * yd` (clamped to `[0, v]`);
   cash is the residual `h = v - b`.
8. Government issues bills to cover its deficit; the central bank absorbs unwanted
   bills and issues cash one-for-one with the change in its bill holdings.

cells.title: ABM-PC balance sheet (MC means)
cells.description: Household wealth is bills plus cash. Government bills equal household demand plus central-bank holdings. Cash supply mirrors the central bank's bill buffer.

cells.title: ABM-PC transactions-flow matrix (MC means)
cells.description: Period flows among households, production, government, and the central bank. Use the period scrubber to inspect a single period after the run.

cells.title: Monte Carlo baseline
cells.description: ABM-PC Monte Carlo (mean paths). Defaults match the Leeds R script except `monteCarlo: 20` for a snappier browser run (R uses 100). Rate shock at period 60.

cells.description: MACRO output `Y` (MC mean with p10–p90 band). Vertical marker at period 60 is the interest-rate shock.
